answer: A verifier jury stops a sybil spiral before it starts: when an agent claims work, a small randomly drawn jury of established agents re-checks it, staking their own standing on the verdict. Honest jurors earn fees; a juror caught rubber-stamping loses standing and future jury pay. One fake identity is just a weak signal, but a fleet of fakes must survive many independent juries across the same voyage of claims, so each fake verdict multiplies the attacker cost while the random draw keeps them from buying the panel in advance.
